summary: Builds a full file path from a directory entry: concatenates the base directory string (entry data +0x144) with the entry name (+0x30) into a path buffer at object +0x10 using an overflow-checked formatter. When the normalize flag at object +0x218 is set, resolves/normalizes the path against an additional path string (object +0x210) via sub_566810 and advances to the end of the final name (handling a trailing backslash). Returns a pointer to the constructed path, or 0 when the enumeration node, entry data, or normalization result is missing.

operations.description: Return 0 when the current enumeration node pointer (object +0x8) is null.
Return 0 when the directory entry data pointer (node +0x0) is null.
Read the base directory string from the entry data at +0x144; fall back to the default application-directory global byte_5EA438 when it is null.
Concatenate base directory and entry name (entry data +0x30) with the '%s%s' format string into the path buffer at object +0x10 via StringFormatWithBufferOverflowCheck.
If the normalize flag byte at object +0x218 is clear, return the pointer to the constructed path buffer at object +0x10.
Read the additional path/filter string from object +0x210; fall back to the default application-directory global byte_5EA438 when it is null.
Normalize/resolve the constructed path buffer against the additional path string via sub_566810.
Return 0 when the path normalization call returned a null pointer.
Advance past the appended additional path using strlen(additional path) + 1; include the trailing backslash byte (0x5C) when the character at that position equals 0x5C.
Return a pointer to the final constructed path (or 0 on any failure path).

unresolved: Exact layout/meaning of the additional path at object +0x210 and the normalize flag at object +0x218 is not confirmed beyond path construction use.
